p.src: Now the monk of Longhua Temple told Song Jiang the name of the peerless Jade Qilin, Lu Junyi. Wu Yong said, “With my persuasive tongue, I can go straight to the Northern Capital and talk Lu Junyi into joining us on the mountain as easily as reaching into a bag for an object. I need only one bold, reckless attendant to accompany me.” Before he had finished, Black Whirlwind Li Kui cried loudly, “Brother Strategist, I’ll make the journey with you!” Song Jiang rebuked him: “Brother, stay where you are! If the task were setting fires upwind, killing downwind, plundering homes, or storming prefectures and cities, you would be just the man for it. But this is the work of a spy. With that temper of yours, you cannot go.” Li Kui said, “You all think I’m ugly. You dislike me and don’t want me along.” Song Jiang said, “It is not that we dislike you. The Daming Prefecture is now teeming with constables. If anyone sees through your disguise, you will only throw away your life.” Li Kui cried, “Never mind! I am determined to go.” Wu Yong said, “If you agree to three conditions of mine, I will take you. If you cannot, remain here in the stronghold.” Li Kui said, “Never mind three—even if there were thirty, I would obey you!” Wu Yong said, “First, drink affects you like blazing fire. From today onward, you must abstain from wine, though you may drink again when we return. Second, on the road you must dress as a Daoist acolyte and follow me, obeying whenever I give you an order. The third is the hardest: beginning tomorrow, you must not speak a single word, but behave as though you were mute. If you can observe these three conditions, I will take you.” Li Kui said, “I can manage not drinking and dressing as a Daoist acolyte; but keeping this mouth shut and saying nothing will suffocate me to death!” Wu Yong said, “The moment you open your mouth, you will cause trouble.” Li Kui said, “That is easy enough. I’ll just hold a copper coin in my mouth!” Song Jiang said, “Brother, if you insist on going, do not blame me should anything go wrong.” Li Kui said, “Never mind, never mind! I’ll take my two broad axes along, and I won’t stop until I’ve hewn off at least a thousand of the bastards’ heads!” All the chieftains laughed; there was no persuading him. That day a farewell banquet was held in the Hall of Loyalty and Righteousness. When evening came, each retired to rest. Early the next morning, Wu Yong packed a bundle of luggage, had Li Kui disguise himself as a Daoist acolyte, and sent him down the mountain carrying the load. Song Jiang and all the chieftains saw them off at Golden Sands Beach, repeatedly urging Wu Yong to be vigilant and not let any harm befall Li Kui. Wu Yong and Li Kui bade farewell to the others and descended the mountain, while Song Jiang and his companions returned to the stronghold.

p.src: Wu Yong and Li Kui now headed for the Northern Capital. They traveled for four or five days, lodging at inns each evening and lighting a fire to prepare food before setting out at dawn. All along the way, Li Kui tormented Wu Yong beyond endurance. After several days, they reached an inn outside the walls of the Northern Capital and stopped there. That evening, Li Kui went to the kitchen to prepare their meal and struck the waiter with one punch, making him cough blood. The waiter came to Wu Yong’s room and complained, “That mute Daoist boy of yours is far too vicious. Just because I was a little slow lighting the fire, he beat me until I spat blood.” Wu Yong hastily apologized and gave him more than ten strings of cash to recuperate with. His private reproaches of Li Kui need not be recounted. The night passed, and at daybreak they rose, prepared some food, and ate. Wu Yong called Li Kui into the room and warned him: “You rogue, you insisted on coming, and you’ve plagued me to death the whole journey! We enter the city today, and it is no place for sport. Do not cost me my life!” Li Kui said, “I would not dare, I would not dare.” Wu Yong said, “Let us arrange another secret signal. If I shake my head, you must not make a move.” Li Kui agreed.

p.src: Wu Yong and Li Kui swaggered along until they reached the city gate. Some forty or fifty soldiers were guarding it, clustered around the gate officer, who sat in their midst. Wu Yong stepped forward and bowed. A soldier asked, “Where have you come from, scholar?” Wu Yong replied, “My humble surname is Zhang, and my given name is Yong. This Daoist acolyte is surnamed Li. I make my living traveling the rivers and lakes, telling fortunes. I have now come to this great prefecture to interpret people’s destinies.” He took a forged travel permit from his person and showed it to the soldiers. The men said, “That Daoist boy’s damned eyes glare at people just like a bandit’s!” Hearing this, Li Kui was about to fly into a rage, but Wu Yong hastily shook his head, and Li Kui lowered his own. Wu Yong stepped forward and apologized to the gate guards: “It is a long and painful tale! This Daoist boy is both deaf and mute and possesses nothing but brute strength. But he is a boy born into my household, so I had no choice but to bring him along. The rogue understands nothing of proper conduct. I beg your pardon!” He took his leave and moved on. Li Kui followed behind, lurching unevenly toward the heart of the marketplace. Shaking the bell and baton in his hand, Wu Yong chanted four lines: “Gan Luo rose early, while Ziya’s hour came late; Peng Zu lived long, while Yan Hui met a brief fate. Fan Dan was poor, while Shi Chong possessed vast treasure; from birth, each person’s destiny ripens in its own measure.” Wu Yong continued, “It is all a matter of time, fortune, and destiny. I know birth and death, nobility and baseness. If you would ask what lies ahead, first bestow one tael of silver.” When he had finished speaking, he shook the bell and baton again. Some fifty or sixty children of the Northern Capital followed them, watching and laughing. They happened to turn up before the pawnshop of Squire Lu. Wu Yong sang and laughed by himself, went away, then returned again, while the children raised a great commotion.

p.src: Wu Yong stepped forward and bowed. Lu Junyi inclined his body in return and asked, “Sir, where is your honored home? What are your honored surname and distinguished name?” Wu Yong replied, “My humble surname is Zhang and my given name is Yong. I style myself the Heaven-Divining Tongue. My ancestral home is in Shandong. I can calculate the cosmic numbers of the Earlier Heaven and discern a person’s life and death, rank and lowliness. Only upon receiving a fee of one tael of silver will I tell a fortune.” Lu Junyi invited him into a small chamber in the rear hall, where host and guest took their appointed seats. When the tea had been drunk, he ordered an attendant to bring one tael of silver and offered it as the divination fee. “May I trouble you, sir, to examine my humble destiny?” Wu Yong said, “Please give me the year, month, day, and hour of your honored birth.” Lu Junyi said, “Sir, a gentleman asks of calamity, not fortune. There is no need to speak of my wealth; I ask only that you calculate what course I should presently follow. I am thirty-two this year, born in a jiazi year, an yichou month, a bingyin day, and a dingmao hour.” Wu Yong took out a set of iron counting rods, arranged them on the table, and calculated for a while. Then he gathered them up, struck the table, and cried, “How strange!” Startled, Lu Junyi asked, “What good or ill does my destiny portend?” Wu Yong said, “If my lord will take no offense, I shall speak plainly.” Lu Junyi replied, “That is precisely why I want you to guide one who has lost his way. Speak without fear.” Wu Yong said, “According to your destiny, my lord, within no more than a hundred days you will surely suffer a bloody calamity. You will be unable to preserve your property and will die beneath sword or blade.” Lu Junyi laughed. “You are mistaken, sir. I, Lu, was born in Beijing and raised in a wealthy household. Among my forefathers not one man broke the law, nor among my kinswomen was there one who married twice. Moreover, I conduct myself cautiously: I do nothing contrary to right and take no wealth that is not mine. How could I possibly suffer a bloody calamity?” Wu Yong’s expression changed. He hastily returned the silver, rose to leave, and sighed, “So everyone beneath heaven wants only flattery and fawning! Enough, enough! I plainly point out the level road, yet loyal counsel is taken for malicious speech. I take my leave.” Lu Junyi said, “Please calm your anger, sir. My earlier words were merely a jest. I sincerely wish to hear your counsel.” Wu Yong said, “I shall speak plainly, but you must on no account take offense!” Lu Junyi replied, “I am listening most attentively. Please conceal nothing.” Wu Yong said, “Your honored destiny, my lord, has always enjoyed good fortune. But this year your hour clashes with the Lord of the Year, and you are entering a baleful cycle. Within a hundred days from now, your head and body will lie apart. This was allotted at your birth and cannot be escaped.” Lu Junyi asked, “Can it be avoided?” Wu Yong arranged the iron counting rods once more. Then he answered Lord Lu, “Only by going a thousand li or more to the southeast, in the direction of Xun, can you escape this great disaster. Though you may suffer some fright, no grave harm will befall you.” Lu Junyi said, “If I can escape this disaster, I shall reward you richly.” Wu Yong said, “Your destiny contains a divinatory verse of four lines. I shall recite it to you, and you should write it on the wall. When it is fulfilled in days to come, you will know the efficacy of my art.” Lu Junyi ordered brush and inkstone brought and went to write upon the whitewashed wall. Wu Yong chanted four lines: “Amid the reed blossoms lies a little boat; a hero soon shall journey from this place. If the righteous man can grasp this truth, turn back, flee disaster, and be free of care.” When Lu Junyi had finished writing, Wu Yong gathered up his counting rods, bowed, and prepared to leave. Lu Junyi urged him to stay. “Sit a while longer, sir, and leave after midday.” Wu Yong replied, “Many thanks for your generous kindness, my lord, but I have already lost time from selling fortunes. I shall visit you again another day.” With that, he withdrew and rose. Lu Junyi escorted him to the gate, while Li Kui took up his crutch-staff and went outside. He had come to Beijing seeking acquaintances but failed to find them and collapsed from cold before Lord Lu’s gate. Lu Junyi saved his life and took him into his household. Finding him diligent and careful, and skilled at writing and reckoning, Lu Junyi set him to manage the household affairs. Within five years, he had promoted him all the way to chief manager. All the household property, inside and out, was placed in his hands. Under him were forty or fifty clerks and agents who handled the finances, and everyone in the household called him Chief Manager Li. p.src: At the sight, Lu Junyi’s heart blazed like fire and his rage rose like smoke. Gripping his staff-sword, he raced straight after them. When he was not far from the hillside, two heroes appeared and shouted, “Where do you think you are going?” One was Zhu Tong, the Lord of the Beautiful Beard; the other was Lei Heng, the Winged Tiger. Seeing them, Lu Junyi cursed loudly, “You band of grass-bandits, return my carts, men, and horses at once!” Zhu Tong stroked his long beard and laughed. “Master Lu, do you still understand so little? Now that you have fallen into our strategist’s brilliant trap, you could not fly out even if wings sprouted from your ribs. Come quickly to the stronghold and take a seat of honor.” Lu Junyi flew into a rage and charged straight at the two men with his staff-sword raised. Zhu Tong and Lei Heng each raised his weapon to meet him. Before three bouts had passed, both men turned and fled. Lu Junyi thought, “I must run down at least one of them before I can recover my convoy.” Risking his life, he chased them around the hillside, but both heroes had vanished. He heard drums and clappers and the sound of flutes on the mountaintop. Looking up, he saw the wind unfurl an apricot-yellow banner embroidered with the four words: “Act on Heaven’s Behalf.” Turning to look, he saw Song Jiang sheltered beneath a red silk, gold-figured parasol, with Wu Yong on his left and Gongsun Sheng on his right. Their retinue of more than two hundred men saluted with one voice: “Master, we trust you have been well since last we met!” The sight only enraged Lu Junyi further, and he pointed up the mountain, cursing them by name. Wu Yong urged him, “Master, please calm your anger for the moment. Song Gongming has long admired your great renown and specially ordered me to visit your residence in person and welcome you up the mountain, so that together we might act on Heaven’s behalf. Please do not blame us.” Lu Junyi cursed furiously, “You wanton grass-bandits! How dare you trick me!” From behind Song Jiang emerged Hua Rong, the “Little Li Guang.” Nocking an arrow to his bow, he stared at Lu Junyi and shouted, “Master Lu, do not flaunt your prowess. First behold Hua Rong’s divine archery!” Before the words had left his mouth, an arrow hissed through the air and struck the red tassel on Lu Junyi’s felt hat. Startled, Lu Junyi turned and fled. Drums thundered on the mountain, shaking the earth. Qin Ming, the Thunderbolt, and Lin Chong, the Panther Head, appeared leading a force of men and horses, waving banners and shouting as they charged out from the eastern side of the mountain. Then Huyan Zhuo, the Double-Whip General, and Xu Ning, the Golden-Lance Bearer, appeared with another force, waving banners and shouting as they charged from the western side of the mountain. Lu Junyi was terrified to find every escape cut off. Night was drawing on; his feet ached and his belly was empty. In his panic he chose no path, but simply fled down a lonely mountain track. Toward dusk, haze blurred the distant waters and mist sealed the deep mountains. Stars and moon shone faintly, and the thickets could scarcely be made out. As he pressed on, if he had not reached the end of heaven, he had surely come to the end of earth. At last he arrived at Duckbill Shoal; looking out, he saw only reed blossoms filling his vision and a boundless waste of misty water. Seeing this, Lu Junyi raised his face to heaven and sighed deeply. “I would not heed the counsel of good men, and today calamity has indeed overtaken me.”

p.src: When the song ended, the men in all three boats called out their greetings together. In the middle was Ruan Xiaoer, on the left Ruan Xiaowu, and on the right Ruan Xiaoqi. The three small boats charged toward them together. At this Lu Junyi grew even more alarmed. Knowing that he could not swim, he repeatedly shouted to the fisherman, “Quick! Bring the boat in to the bank!” The fisherman laughed aloud and said to Lu Junyi, “Above us is the blue sky, and below us the green water. I was born on the Xunyang River and came here to Liangshan Marsh. At the third watch I do not change my name, nor at the fourth my surname: I am Li Jun, nicknamed the River-Dragon!” If you still refuse to submit, Master Lu, you will merely throw your life away!” Lu Junyi was greatly startled. With a roar he cried, “Either you die or I do!” Gripping his long-handled saber, he thrust it at Li Jun’s heart. As the blade came at him, Li Jun steadied the steering board, flipped backward in a somersault, and plunged into the water with a splash. The boat spun round and round on the surface, and the saber thrust down into the water after him. Just then a man surfaced from beneath the water at the stern. With a shout he revealed himself as Zhang Shun, the White Streak in the Waves. Clamping one arm around the stern and treading the waves with his feet, he tipped the boat onto its side until its bottom faced the sky, and the hero fell into the water. Indeed, they had laid a scheme to snare phoenix and cage dragon, and dug a pit for a man who could shake heaven and earth. What ultimately became of Lu Junyi’s life will be revealed in the next chapter.
